notes.text: The vocalization is based on the JBA and Mandaic spellings, as well as the Arabic loan pilizzun with final double consonant. Since the etymology of this Mediterranean culture word is otherwise unknown, and the initial labial varies between /p/ and /b/, we would suggest an origin from a hypothetical Assyrian bu/illiltu, from the root balālu, "to mix;" compare billu A, "alloy, melt." For the phonological correspondences compare discussions s.v. mlš div. and zbn n.m.#2.
